title: Indirect Addressing: An Address That Points at an Address
quickIdea: Indirect mode reads a pointer first: the instruction names a location, and that location holds the effective address. Two operand memory references buy a much larger address space.
remember: Effective address = [address field]: read the named location, and what you read is the address of the operand.
Two operand memory references, not one: one to fetch the pointer, one to fetch the operand.
The reach is not the field width but the word width: an n-bit word gives 2^n addresses even when the field is short.
It is the mode for pointers, for passing an array by reference, and for any access whose target address is computed at run time.
Its cost is the extra memory reference and the extra latency, which is why a compiler keeps the pointer in a register (register indirect) when it can.
Multi-level indirection (a pointer to a pointer) simply adds another read per level.

example.prompt: An instruction has an 8-bit address field holding 200, M[200] = 1500 and M[1500] = 42. What does an indirect-mode operand give, and how many memory reads does it take?
example.work: Read M[200] to get 1500 - that is the effective address - then read M[1500] to get 42. Two reads.
example.answer: The operand is 42, reached in two memory reads, from an 8-bit field that alone could only have named 256 locations.

gateAngle: GATE CSE 1999 Q.2.23 is the mode-power question: with only immediate and direct addressing, which language features are out of reach? Pointers need indirection, and arrays, records and recursive-procedure locals are all reached through a computed address, so the accepted answer is all four. The memory-cycle cost of indirection is the second half: GATE CSE 2005 Q.65 charges an indirect operand two reads and an indexed operand one.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: A processor has only immediate and direct modes. Can it implement a linked list traversal?
variations.answer: Not in the ordinary way: following a next pointer needs the address to come from memory, which is indirection. It can only be done by self-modifying code, which most ISAs forbid.
variations.why: This is the same argument the 1999 question makes for pointers, applied to a concrete data structure.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why does indirect addressing widen the address space without widening the instruction?
variations.answer: Because the pointer stored in memory is a full word wide, while the field that names the pointer is only as wide as the instruction allows.
variations.why: The instruction supplies a small address; the machine supplies the rest of the width from the word it reads. This is the exact trade against direct addressing.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: How many memory reads does a two-level indirect operand take, and what does each one deliver?
variations.answer: Three: the pointer's pointer, the pointer, then the operand.
variations.why: Each level of indirection is one more dependent read, which is why deep pointer chains are slow even on machines that support them.

trap.what: Counting one memory reference for indirect mode.
trap.why: The pointer is itself in memory, so the effective address is not known until a read completes.
trap.counterexample: Register indirect needs one read, because the pointer is already in a register; memory indirect needs two. GATE distinguishes the two precisely by this count.

check.question: An 8-bit address field holds 40, M[40] = 9000 and M[9000] = 5. What is the indirect operand, and how many memory reads does it take?
check.explanation: The first read takes M[40] = 9000, which is the effective address; the second takes M[9000] = 5, which is the operand. The 8-bit field alone could only have named 256 locations, so indirection has widened the reach to the word width.

sourceLine: The indirect rung, described as the instruction naming a location which in turn names the data, and the note that indirection is what expands the reachable space: Deka et al., Lecture 12 (English, read in part). The statement, translated from Hindi, that indirect mode needs three or more memory references for the whole instruction and reaches 2^N addresses for an N-bit word: computernetworksite.in (Hindi, translated, read in part). The two-read operand count used on this card is the operand half of that figure, and the distinction is stated in scripts/validate.py.
